subject: Support coverage & response ladder proposal for Acme Data
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@acmedata.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: samir.p@acmedata.com, legal@acmedata.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Support coverage & response ladder proposal for Acme Data

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. Before our procurement review next Friday I need to align on two pieces we discussed with the engineering and legal teams:

1) Response ladder and on-call coverage: we need a clear definition for P1/P2/P3 SLAs, expected response times, and which hours are covered by the standard plan vs. a paid retainer. Our product team will require 24/7 escalation for P1s and a faster callback SLA for P2s during business hours.

2) Pricing & credits: Acme is asking for a structured uptime credit schedule tied to monthly availability and an associated discount for committing to a higher monthly spend. We are also evaluating whether a regional failover guarantee (US -> EU) is included or if that should be an add-on.

Can you share a formal packaging option that maps response windows to price bands and shows the incremental cost for 24/7 on-call plus the discount tiers for 12/18 month commits? If you can include an example DocuSign amendment and a simple one-page summary we can circulate to our CFO and legal.

Thanks —
Elena
Elena Morales
VP, Infrastructure
Acme Data

[Attachment: Acme-Support-Questions.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet) - 34 KB]

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena@acmedata.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, samir.p@acmedata.com, legal@acmedata.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Support coverage & response ladder proposal for Acme Data

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached is a concise packaging proposal that maps three priority tiers to response windows, escalation paths, and pricing bands. High level:

- Standard: 9x5 business-hours support, P1 initial response < 2 hours, P2 < 4 hours, P3 < 24 hours. Included with hosted plans.
- Priority Retainer (recommended): 24/7 P1 coverage, guaranteed engineer follow-up within 30 minutes for P1s, P2 follow-up within 2 hours during business hours; retainer is monthly and credits are applied against incident work.
- Enterprise Plus: Priority Retainer + regional failover SLA (active-active failover runbook + quarterly failover tests) and an uptime credit ladder that starts at 99.9% with increasing credits at 99.5/99.0 thresholds.

Pricing examples (monthly commit):
- No commit: Priority Retainer = $8,000 / month, Enterprise Plus = +$6,000 / month
- 12-month commit (20% platform credit): Priority Retainer = $6,400 / month
- 18-month commit (25% platform credit): Priority Retainer = $6,000 / month + 1 free annual failover test

We can show a blended discount for CPU/GPU committed capacity if you prefer to fold infra spend into the same commitment — I flagged that for Aditya to propose a margin-safe discount.

Attachments: redwood-priority-bundles-v2.pdf (one-page summary) and a sample DocuSign amendment (template) for SLA changes. If you want, we can prepare an ACME-specific amendment and the legal-friendly language for the uptime credit ladder.

Next step: I suggest a 30-minute call with Aditya (commercial) and Vanessa (ops) to lock the exact retainer cadence and failover requirements. When would your team be available Thursday or Friday?

Best,
Sofia Ivánova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0191

[Attachment: redwood-priority-bundles-v2.pdf (application/pdf) - 120 KB]
[Attachment: DocuSign-SLA-Amendment-Acme.pdf (application/pdf) - 80 KB]

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena@acmedata.com>, sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, samir.p@acmedata.com, legal@acmedata.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Support coverage & response ladder proposal for Acme Data

Elena / team —

Following Sofia's note, I ran the numbers against our capacity planning and margin targets and we can move on a stronger commitment:

Offer update (binding if accepted via DocuSign amendment):
- 18-month committed spend at >= $120k/month: 18% platform discount on list rates + complimentary annual failover test (Enterprise Plus).
- 12-month committed spend at >= $90k/month: 15% platform discount + reduced retainer (Priority Retainer = $5,440 / month after discount).
- Uptime credit ladder: credits expressed as % of monthly invoice with a max cap equal to one month's retail value; credits increase at 99.8%, 99.5%, 99.0% with tiered percentages (details in attached PDF).
- P1 definitions and measurements: P1 = production-complete outage impacting >10% requests or a critical API path; response SLA is 30 minutes to acknowledge and begin mitigation; restoration target remains workload-dependent but we commit to escalation timelines and on-call engineer assignment.

We can also include a 30-day pilot clause with a reduced early-termination fee if you follow our observability checklist (helps prevent noisy incidents from skewing SLO measurements).

If this looks good, Sofia can spin the DocuSign fully-populated with the ACME account values and I will route for an expedited executive approval on our end.

Link to the redline-ready amendment and the pricing worksheet: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-RED-2026-Q4

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk legal through the uptime credit language.

—Aditya Rao
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
